title.narrative: Urban Services Improvement Investment Program - Tranche 5

description.narrative: Project 5 will finance the sewerage system in Zugdidi and Mestia, the secondary towns covered by the Investment Program. The first component of the project will support infrastructure investments to construct sewerage system in Zugdidi and Mestia, and benefit approximately 20,600 households in Zugdidi and a population of 6,500 in Mestia (including floating tourist population). The second component will include project implementation support.

Data Source: 2a. to 2b. - Semiannual progress reports prepared by UWSCG, PPMS reports prepared by UWSCG, UWSCG annual work plans Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2023 Target value: Y

a. Residents' access to safe sanitation increased from Nil in 2013 to 100% in 2021 for Zugdidi through provision of sewer connections to all existing 20,600 households. Progress/Status: Zugdidi wastewater network project is on defects notification period which will end on 2 Aug 2020.
The completion certificate for the Zugdidi wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) contract was issued on 19 Feb 2021.
The contract for Mestia WWTP (Design-Build) was awarded on 8 Nov 2019 and Contractor was deployed on 12 Dec 2019. Due to high dilution of wastewater, the technology for treatment was proposed to be changed, i.e., cancel and postpone the construction of the biological part of the WWTP. UWSCG requested reduction of scope of the contract to the design services only. Request is under consideration of ADB. Government plans to construct the WWTP once high consumption of the water is resolved.
Due to delays, it is expected that the contract will be extended from the current completion of 4 June 2021. Request to extend DNP until end of October 2021 was sent to ADB in 11 October 2021. UWSCG considers further extension of DNP until 31 December 2021. Submission of no objection request is expected by 15 November 2021.
Based on the request of the Government, construction of Mestia WWTP has been removed from the scope of the porject. Data Source: a. National statistics on water supply quality and effluent discharge from MOEPA and UWSCG Actual value:

b. 100% households headed by women in the region covered by 2024 Progress/Status: 100% female-headed households are confirmed to benefit from the projects in Zugdidi.
The project benefit, particularly to female-headed households, is delayed in Mestia due to removal of WWTP from project scope. Data Source: b.
